title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study measuring whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, ≤1 repair) reduces invariant violations versus single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and an automated network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed all verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n10 = 1, n01 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report the preregistration, execution artifacts, paired analysis, a failure-mode diagnosis, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational safety requires that generated configurations satisfy deterministic invariants such as reachability, policy compliance, loop‑freedom, and ordered-change/workflow constraints. Prior work has explored intent→configuration prototypes and the need for verification [1], and separate literature develops deterministic verifiers for configuration validation [2]. Cross-domain studies advocate pairing generation with external validators and repair loops to mitigate unsafe outputs in program-repair and related tasks [4]. Reporting guidelines recommend preregistration and artifact disclosure to improve reproducibility for LLM studies [3].

This study asks: under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes), to what extent does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (one permitted repair call) reduce invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation? We answer with a preregistered paired evaluation (N = 200 tasks) executed with a deterministic synthetic task generator, a deterministic network verifier, and the hosted LLM gpt-5-mini, with all run artifacts archived.
sections.related_work: Intent→configuration and NetOps-focused LLM evaluations have produced prototype pipelines and task banks assessing whether models can synthesize device configurations from natural-language intents [1]. Deterministic verifiers and formal validators have been used to check reachability and policy properties for configurations in prior network-verification work [2]. Cross-domain evidence from program repair and tool-augmented LLM agents shows that generate→validate→repair patterns can improve verifiability in software engineering contexts [4],[6]. Survey and safety literature document LLM failure modes and recommend verifier stages and provenance controls for operational deployments [5],[3]. Our experiment places a tightly controlled, verifier-centered empirical test with archived artifacts alongside these prior threads.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration: Study CAND-2026-001 was preregistered before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — per-task binary indicator that the deterministic verifier accepts the generated configuration (all specified invariants pass).

Sampling and tasks: 200 deterministic intent→configuration tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 targeting very_hard and extreme workflow patterns. Inclusion/exclusion rules and deterministic selection indices were fixed in the preregistration.

Generation semantics and model configuration: The preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial generation was sampled per task and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes; independent first-pass generations per condition were not produced. The declared execution model was gpt-5-mini; the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task.

Execution and verifier: The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter performed model calls and orchestration. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed full intent-constraint validation: syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, encoded workflow/ordering policies, and network-level invariants. Per-task outcome was binary: 'all invariants pass' versus 'any invariant fails'.

Analysis: Primary confirmatory test was an exact McNemar-style paired test with discordant-pair reporting. Per-condition pass rates use 95% Wilson CIs. Paired bootstrap percentile CI for the risk difference used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis plan and failure-handling rules followed the preregistration; sensitivity analyses treating persistent unparsables as failures were prepared but not invoked because no persistent unparsables occurred.
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed per preregistration (planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400). Provider/audit accounting appears in the archived execution manifest.

Primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (rows: guarded; columns: baseline). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the difference = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Repair activity and failure diagnosis: The guarded pipeline invoked its single permitted repair once; that repair converted the sole baseline failure into a guarded success. The archived validator trace for the repaired task indicates a multi-step ordering/workflow constraint crossing interfaces (a required sequence violation). The repair produced a corrected sequence that satisfied the verifier's encoded invariants; the verifier accepted the repaired candidate.

Missingness and exclusions: No preregistered exclusions occurred; no unparsable persistent outputs or failed episodes were observed under the prespecified handling rules.
sections.discussion:
Scientific interpretation: In this synthetic task corpus with the chosen verifier and gpt-5-mini, single-shot generation already satisfied verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks; a single bounded repair corrected the remaining multi-step ordering error. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, the paired difference arises solely from verifier-triggered repair rather than independent first-pass generation differences. Thus the executed estimand measures the effect of the verifier/repair stage only.

Statistical perspective: The preregistration targeted detecting a 10–15 percentage-point absolute change assuming mid-range baseline rates (~45–65%); the observed baseline (~99.5%) was far higher than anticipated, so the original power assumptions do not apply. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 reflects that with only one discordant pair (n10 = 1 and n01 = 0) the small-sample exact paired test cannot reject the null; the paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies the realized detectable improvement given this run.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is limited by shared_initial_candidate semantics (no independent first-pass contrast), potential oracle incompleteness, and a single-model evaluation. Construct validity: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but cannot observe runtime behaviors visible only via live-device execution. External validity: tasks are synthetic and topologies controlled; adversarial contamination was not exercised. Practical implication: verifier gates with bounded repair can remediate specific ordering faults in a constrained synthetic corpus, but broader operational claims require multi-model, more diverse tasks, independent first-pass comparisons, adversarial testing, or live-device evaluation.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-guarded intent→configuration pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. With gpt-5-mini on the supplied synthetic task bank, single-shot generation produced very high verifier compliance (199/200), and a single verifier-triggered repair converted the sole failing case into success, giving a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points) with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015]. The archival bundle documents the end-to-end generator→validator→repair pipeline and all analysis artifacts to support reproducibility. Future work should evaluate multiple models, larger/diverse task banks (including noisy or partial state and live-device semantics), independent first-pass comparisons when required by the estimand, adversarial contamination, and richer runtime oracles.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task; detailed execution accounting and archived artifacts (provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, and per-file hashes) are available in the archived execution manifest (see execution/execution_manifest.json in the artifact bundle). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent prompt-engineering or constrained-generation effects.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
